canonical_claim.safe_public_wording: Sley is an agent-native structural programming language for compiler-mediated, human-reviewed software change.
canonical_claim.disputed_search_phrase: world's first fully AI-native programming language, built by AI for AI
canonical_claim.proof_boundary: The public repository verifies Sley's language-design and implementation-stage claims. It does not prove complete global firstness or strict self-hosting.

required_criteria.name: Independent language substrate
required_criteria.description: Sley has its own source form, semantic model, checked command surface, and runtime or execution contract.

required_criteria.name: Compiler-owned structural model
required_criteria.description: Typed program structure is exposed through first-class machine contracts instead of raw text inference.

required_criteria.name: Native agent edit path
required_criteria.description: Inspection, diagnostics, planned repairs, structural grafts, verification, traces, and seals are compiler-mediated surfaces.

required_criteria.name: Deterministic authority gates
required_criteria.description: Host-facing effects are explicit, bounded, and reproducible without live host calls in the public proof path.

required_criteria.name: Independent auditability
required_criteria.description: A clean public checkout includes exact local commands that verify the current claimed stage without private infrastructure.

evidence.claim: The public self-hosting gate blocks forbidden foreign-language implementation files.
A runnable stage-1 Sley command surface exists under bin/.
Sley-owned stage-2 semantic source modules exist and are reported by the CLI.
Selected bootstrap, parser, checker, lint, runtime, and report-shape values are read from .sley source.
Structural inspection is exposed through stable JSON roots, schemas, and contract fixtures.
Structural edits can be checked before mutation through dry-run graft previews.
Authority-gated effects are modeled deterministically without live secret, network, spend, or deploy calls.
The local v1 gate is reproducible from a public checkout.
The claim boundary, criteria, evidence paths, prior-art candidates, and public gates are machine-checkable.
The public release remains blocked until strict Sley-written parity, a proof bundle, and operator approval are present.

candidates.classification: Current strongest match among the reviewed candidates, but not final strict self-hosting.
Adaptive/runtime-native language, not proven agent-native structural language under Sley's criteria.
Serious AI-native language, but not the same category as Sley's structural edit contract in the reviewed docs.
AI-oriented title claimant focused on one-correct-way syntax and token reduction, not shown to satisfy Sley's structural criteria.
High-performance Python implementation/compiler and name-collision note, not the Codong claimant.
Agent framework, not an independent programming-language substrate in this comparison category.
AI-infrastructure/system language, not Sley-style agent-native structural programming in the reviewed docs.

blockers: strict Sley-written semantic parity is not complete
public proof bundle is not approved
operator has not approved public release or external issue text
